approach: Judge a pull request's checks by the one required check name and report the rest as notes. In gh/client.rs, `classify_checks` stops treating any failed check-run as red. It looks only at the check-run named by `CI_AGGREGATE_JOB` ("fmt, clippy, tests"), which becomes `pub(super)` and is the one source of the name. It is Red if that run failed, Pending if it is missing or unfinished, and Green if it succeeded or was skipped. A new `PrHost::optional_failures(commit)` has a default of "none". `GhClient` implements it by reading the same check-runs and statuses and returning the failed names that are not required. `land_pr` calls it once after the wait and adds each name to `PrReport.warnings` as a note: "not required by main, so not a failure". `warnings` is already documented as non-failure notes. The drain's `PrLander` is unchanged. With a green required check, `land_pr` merges and reports Landed, so the drain never sees `NotLanded` and never counts a failure. The thrash-stop rule is untouched. In gate/invariant.rs, `classify_pre_merge` stops treating a job as claiming a landing when the job's records in the commit tree have no verification, no `outcome.json` and no later outcome (a held job: candidate, invocations and plans only). That commit then falls through to the existing intervention, fingerprint and records-only rules. A job with an outcome and no verification still returns `NoVerification`.

decisions.choice: Fix the check judgment in `classify_checks` (client.rs), where Red is made, by naming the required check, and keep the `PrHost::checks` signature.
decisions.reason: The fault starts where any failed run becomes Red. Fixing it there corrects the landing wait, its rerun logic and the refusal text together, and no fake host has to change.

rejected.option: Map the optional red to a drain-side exception in `PrLander` or drain.rs
rejected.why: That treats the symptom. The wait would still rerun and report Red, and the thrash-stop rule is out of scope.

rejected.option: Change `Checks` to carry the optional names
rejected.why: `Checks` is `Copy` and used by many fake hosts and display code. A separate default trait method is smaller.

decisions.choice: The required-name set is the existing `CI_AGGREGATE_JOB` constant. Make it `pub(super)` and point `EARLY_RUN_JOB` in early.rs at it. Use a one-element `const REQUIRED_CHECKS: [&str; 1] = [CI_AGGREGATE_JOB]` only if the classifier wants a slice.
decisions.reason: Criterion 7 needs one source. early.rs currently repeats the literal, so referencing the constant removes a duplicate.

rejected.option: Read the names from ci.yml or xtask's REQUIRED_CHECK_NAME at run time
rejected.why: xtask's constant is in a test file of another crate, and parsing the workflow adds machinery. The xtask test already ties its constant to the workflow.

decisions.choice: Ignore combined-status contexts when judging and list only failed ones in the note. Treat a check-run with no name as not required.
decisions.reason: Main requires only the named job. Judging by anything else is the bug. A missing required run stays Pending, so nothing is merged early.

rejected.option: Keep the status-state failure as Red
rejected.why: A failing non-required status context would reproduce the stop.

decisions.choice: Decide 'held job' in `classify_pre_merge`, not in `closing_jobs`. A closing job counts as a landing claim only if it has a verification, an outcome or a later outcome. If none of the three exist, the commit is not a landing claim.
decisions.reason: The brief names `classify_pre_merge`. `closing_jobs` is documented to keep outcome-less jobs so `landing()` can refuse a squash that lands one, so changing it would alter that refusal. The hold's records have candidate and invocations but no outcome and no verification (disk.rs, third and fourth hold places), so the job's own records identify it. The local hold marker is outside the tree and cannot be used.

rejected.why: It is state-dir data, absent from the commit tree and from a pull request check.

rejected.option: Skip the verification check for every job that has a candidate
rejected.why: A finished job's closing records without verification must still fail.

decisions.choice: Test the checks end to end by driving the real `GhClient` over a scripted `Runner` through `land_pr`, with a new fixture next to `FakeRunner`.
decisions.reason: A scripted `FakeHost` returns `Checks` directly, so it cannot show that a red optional run is ignored. A runner that serves check-run JSON puts the production classifier under the test.

rejected.option: Only extend `FakeHost` with an optional-red list
rejected.why: That would test the doubles, not the classifier.

steps: Read gh/client.rs 40-120 (the `PrHost` trait) and 766-794, and the gh/mod.rs re-exports. Make `CI_AGGREGATE_JOB` `pub(super)` and set `EARLY_RUN_JOB` in early.rs to it.

Rewrite `classify_checks` to look only at check-runs named `CI_AGGREGATE_JOB`. Its states: failed conclusions are Red; missing or not completed is Pending; success or skipped is Green. Statuses are not judged. Keep the public name and signature; add a helper that lists the failed non-required run and status names.
Add `PrHost::optional_failures(&self, commit) -> Result<Vec<String>>` with a default of `Ok(vec![])`. Implement it in `GhClient` by reading the same two replies and calling the helper.

In `land_pr` (landing.rs), after the wait, when the pull request is still open and the wait is over, call `optional_failures(&link.head)`. Ignore an error, as the failing-test lookup does. risks.risk: Fixtures that return an unnamed check-run (tests.rs:86, 677-690, and possibly test_support.rs) read Pending once the required name matters.
risks.mitigation: Step 5 renames them to the required name and runs the whole `cargo test -p athena-core`. Keep the `classify_checks(runs, status)` signature.

risks.risk: Ignoring statuses could let a genuinely failing status context through.
risks.mitigation: Main requires only the named job, so judging statuses was the bug. Failing contexts appear in the note, and the required run is still Pending when missing.

risks.risk: The held-job rule could let a job that lost its outcome record slip into history without verification.
risks.mitigation: The commit still has to pass the governed-fingerprint rules, so any governed change returns `GovernedChange`. A finished or landed job has an outcome record and so still returns `NoVerification`.

risks.risk: The extra `optional_failures` API read adds a call to `land_pr`, which could break call-count assertions (for example `check_reads`).
risks.mitigation: The default method makes no call for fake hosts. Only `GhClient` reads, and only once after the wait. The test at tests.rs:106 counts calls, so update its expected count.

risks.risk: Scope creep into land.rs, run/mod.rs and docs.
risks.mitigation: Touch only what the change needs; land.rs and run/mod.rs are conditional. The decision entry records the root cause.

demonstrations.method: A new test in gh/tests.rs, `a_red_optional_check_does_not_fail_the_landing`. It runs `land_pr` through `Rig::run_with` with a `GhClient` over a new scripted runner. The runner serves check-runs `[{name:"fmt, clippy, tests", success}, {name:"pull request head", failure}]`, an unmerged pull request until the merge PUT, then a merged one with commit `merged1`. It uses `merge_via_rest` true, and also false for the waiting case.
demonstrations.observes: The report has `checks == Some(Checks::Green)`, `reruns == 0`, `link.state == Landed` and `merge_requested`. Nothing is `Red`, so `PrLander::land` returns `Landing::Landed` and drain.rs:1537 `failures` is never incremented. With the setting off the report is Open and Green, and nothing failed. The stop is reached only through `NotLanded`, drain.rs:1445-1449 and 1537-1539, which this path never takes.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without required-only judgment, `classify_checks` returns Red for the failed 'pull request head' run, the wait reruns, the report is Red and Open and nothing merges, so the Landed and Green assertions fail.

The new runner is added by plan step 5. `Rig`, `FakeContent` and `GhClient::new(&runner, ..)` exist (tests.rs:56-93, 915-991).
